LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.3: Rhythm and pattern making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and pattern making, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are rhythms created?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and pattern making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: The learner creates simple rhythmic patterns using short and long sounds.

• Self- efficacy: The learner confidently plays rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner in groups, draws geometric basic shapes on the ground and moves in

rhythm on the shapes drawn.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes care of the digital devices as they record the rhythmic chant performances for future use.

• Respect: The learner gives chance to peers as they take turns to recite short and long sounds using French rhythm names.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Life skills: The learner applies skills acquired to safely and rhythmically move while skipping, sliding and galloping

around basic shapes drawn on the ground.

• Social cohesion: The learner portrays team spirit as they work with peers to recite short and long sounds using French

rhythm names.

Link to other learning areas:

11

Mathematics: The learner applies knowledge and skill gained in Mathematics to count and maintain the beat as they move in

rhythm on the shapes drawn to accompany a familiar song.

Suggested learning resources

Colour, printing blocks, digital devices with assistive technologies for the Deaf, musical instruments, pictures, reference books

, audio/video clips of recorded rhythm, relevant virtual sites, relevant props and costumes, resource persons
